summary.text: Carolyn Moore is the Animal Justice Party candidate for Carrum at the 2026 Victorian election. She grew up in East Gippsland and later moved to Melbourne's south-east. She works as an NDIS support worker and holds a mental health diploma, and her party profile says she fosters rescue dogs and volunteers in wildlife rescue.

priorities.text: Phasing out intensive factory farming, with independent monitoring to expose cruelty
Help for farmers to switch to plant-based production, funded by redirecting government support
An immediate end to native forest logging, with transition support for affected communities
Greater spending on mental health care and on services for people with disability

sources.title: Carrum - VIC Election 2026, ABC News election guide
Carolyn Moore for Carrum, Animal Justice Party Victoria

summary.text: Harley Mackenzie is the Legalise Cannabis candidate for Carrum at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC says he has spent about forty years working in the energy sector and in public policy, and that he runs his own software company. At the 2025 federal election he stood for the party in Corangamite.

previous_candidacies.note: The ABC records the candidacy but not the result; Lost is inferred because he did not become the member.

summary.text: Jeff Shelley is the Liberal candidate for Carrum at the 2026 Victorian election. He founded 123Read2me, a local charity working on early childhood literacy, and leads the Lions Club in his area as its president. In 2013 the Liberals endorsed him for the federal seat of Isaacs, but he withdrew before polling day.

sources.title: Carrum - VIC Election 2026, ABC News election guide

summary.text: Joshua Mathews is One Nation's candidate for Carrum at the 2026 Victorian election. The ABC says he has worked as a school bus driver in his family's construction business. He has studied legal practice at Victoria University, at advanced diploma level.

sources.title: Carrum - VIC Election 2026, ABC News election guide

summary.text: Reema Ababneh is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Carrum at the 2026 Victorian state election. On her party page she describes herself as a local resident raised by a single mother. She says she is running so that society is organised around the needs of working-class people, and to oppose racism and the far right.

priorities.text: Real change has never come from waiting for politicians to do the right thing.
Secure housing, good health care and education, and a decent living standard for everyone
Action on rising rents, wages falling behind and the cost of living
Opposing racism and the far right, including politicians who blame migrants and refugees for social problems

sources.title: Carrum: VIC electorate, candidates, results, ABC News

summary.text: Sonya Kilkenny has represented Carrum for Labor in the Legislative Assembly since she won the seat in 2014. A commercial lawyer before entering Parliament, she has been Attorney-General since December 2024 and Planning Minister since 2022, and added Prevention of Family Violence in August 2026. She is recontesting Carrum in 2026.

prior_roles.role: Minister for Prevention of Family Violence
Minister for Finance; Minister for Violence Reduction
Minister for Corrections, Youth Justice, Victim Support, and Fishing and Boating
Parliamentary Secretary for Early Childhood Education
Board member, Back to Back Theatre and the National Theatre

priorities.text: Fair access to services close to home
Jobs of the future, through education and training
Moving the energy sector to renewables
More opportunities for women in work
Technology, innovation and local manufacturing

summary.text: Trevor Smith is the Libertarian candidate for Carrum at the 2026 Victorian election. He is an engineering geologist and runs marathons in his spare time. He contested the federal seat of Casey in 2022 for the Liberal Democrats, the party's former name.

previous_candidacies.note: The ABC records the candidacy (as Liberal Democrats) but not the result; Lost is inferred because he did not become the member.

priorities.text: Free speech and lower taxes
Legal use of pepper spray for self-defence
A right for householders to protect their families from intruders
Less government intrusion on individual rights

summary.text: Zoe Pegrum is the Greens candidate for Carrum at the 2026 Victorian election. She lives in Chelsea Heights and works in hospitality. Beyond that, neither her party page nor the ABC had published biographical details as of November 2026.

priorities.text: I want to represent the every day person in my electorate
Cost-of-living relief paid for by taxing billionaires
Free and frequent public transport, along with more public housing and NDIS support
Showing young people they can become community leaders
